en.Katliam, Çeçen halkını her zamankinden f: The massacre united the Chechen people as never before: every young man is heading for the hills. The world press looks not at Grozny but at Samashki.
en.7–8 Nisan'da Rus iç birliklerinin Samaşk: On 7–8 April Russian interior troops' 'mopping-up' in Samashki killed hundreds of civilians. The Council of Europe froze Russia's membership process; the village sweeps do the most damage to Russia's image.
en.Rehineler için geçit ve ateşkes görüşmes: Safe passage for hostages and ceasefire talks
en.Çernomırdin–Basayev pazarlığıyla rehinel: The Chernomyrdin–Basayev bargain freed the hostages; a military accord was signed on 30 June.
en.Moskova pazarlığı reddetti; hastane ikin: Moscow refused to bargain; the hospital was stormed a second time.
en.Kremlin ağır bir darbe aldı: 'sonuna kad: The Kremlin took a heavy blow: a choice between 'war to the end' and the lives of 1,500 civilians.
en.Basayev'in adamları çıkış koridoruyla da: Basayev's men returned to the mountains through a corridor; the door to negotiations opened.
en.Dudayev kamuoyuna rehinelerin serbest bı: Dudayev publicly called for the hostages' release.
en.Basayev'in baskını savaşın seyrini değiş: Basayev's raid may change the course of the war: Moscow will either back down or look brutal to its own people. But taking civilian hostages isolates you diplomatically.
en.14 Haziran: Şamil Basayev komutasındaki: 14 June: about 150 fighters under Shamil Basayev seized the hospital in Budyonnovsk, Stavropol, taking 1,500 hostages. A Russian special forces assault failed; Prime Minister Chernomyrdin negotiated with Basayev by phone.
en.Moskova Zavgayev'in hükümetini tanıdı; G: Moscow recognised Zavgayev's government; security in Grozny was tightened.
en.Seçim sonrası yeni taarruz: A new offensive after the elections
en.Genelkurmay kış taarruzu için takviye is: The General Staff requested reinforcements for a winter offensive.
en.Seçim kampanyası başlıyor. Yeltsin'in re: The election campaign begins. Yeltsin's ratings are at rock bottom; Zavgayev's 'Chechen government' is a facade but may be an interim solution.
en.Çeçen komutanlar seçimi 'sahte' ilan ett: Chechen commanders declared the vote a 'sham'.
en.Kuzey Kafkasya'ya baskın: Gudermes ve Kı: Raid the North Caucasus: prepare Gudermes and Kizlyar
en.Salman Radüyev'in müfrezeleri kuzeye haz: Salman Raduyev's detachments prepare to move north.
en.Gudermes baskını Rus garnizonunu sarstı: The Gudermes raid shook the Russian garrison but Zavgayev's vote gives Moscow a legal fig leaf. There is pressure in the villages to 'take part'.
en.Aralık 1995: Çeçenler Gudermes'i kısa sü: December 1995: the Chechens briefly held Gudermes while Russia held Duma elections and a 'head of administration' vote in Chechnya. Moscow's man, Doku Zavgayev, 'won', but most Chechens did not recognise the vote.
en.Müzakere ve diplomasiyle kaçırıcılar 19: Through negotiation the hijackers released the hostages and surrendered on 19 January; Russia thanked Turkey.
en.Ankara komandoları Boğaz'da alarma geçir: Ankara put commandos on alert in the Bosphorus; the crisis grew dangerously tense.
en.Çeçen davasına anlayış göster: Show understanding for the Chechen cause
en.Kaçırıcılarla görüş, kamuoyu mesajı: Talk to hijackers, send a public message
en.Ankara kaçırıcıların taleplerini dinleye: Ankara said it would hear the hijackers' demands; Moscow reacted angrily.
en.Karadeniz'de 200 kadar yolcusu ve çok sa: A Turkish ferry with some 200 passengers, many of them Russian citizens, was hijacked on the Black Sea and is heading for the Bosphorus. Relations with Russia and domestic opinion are in a delicate balance.
en.Rus topçusu köyü haftalarca dövdü; Radüy: Russian artillery shelled the village for days; Raduyev broke through and escaped.
en.Moskova Dağıstan hükümeti aracılığıyla p: Moscow bargained through the Dagestani authorities.
en.Radüyev'in Kızlyar baskını Dağıstan'ı sa: Raduyev's Kizlyar raid pulls Dagestan into the war; shelling Pervomayskoye with hostages inside became a bloody fiasco. It is Yeltsin's election year.
en.Çeçen komutanlar baskını 'Rusya'nın kalb: Chechen commanders presented the raid as 'a message to the heart of Russia'.
en.Dudayev'in danışmanları baskını 'bağımsı: Dudayev's advisers described the raid as an 'independent action'.
en.Radüyev Dudayev'in akrabası ve 'ordu gen: Raduyev is Dudayev's relative and a self-styled army general; the raid gave you prestige but frightened the people of Dagestan.
en.9 Ocak: Radüyev Dağıstan'ın Kızlyar kent: 9 January: Raduyev raided Kizlyar in Dagestan, took 3,000 hostages and fell back on Pervomayskoye, which Russian artillery flattened. On 16 January the Turkish ferry Avrasya (Trabzon–Sochi) was hijacked in the name of the Chechen cause; the hijackers surrendered in Istanbul on 19 January.
en.Yeltsin 31 Mart planını genişletip Çeçen: Yeltsin broadened his 31 March plan and offered fresh talks to the Chechens.
en.Rus birlikleri komutanları hedef alan ye: Russian forces began new offensives targeting commanders.
en.Dudayev'in ölümü Yeltsin'e seçim öncesi: Dudayev's death gives Yeltsin a pre-election success; but the resistance does not end with its leader. A window for a peace plan has opened.
en.Maskhadov bütün sahra komutanlığını üstl: Maskhadov took over all field command.
en.Dudayev şehit düştü; halk yastayken Yand: Dudayev is dead; as the people mourn, a struggle for influence among Yandarbiyev, Maskhadov and Basayev may begin.
en.21 Nisan 1996: Cahar Dudayev uydu telefo: 21 April 1996: Dzhokhar Dudayev was killed by a guided missile from a Russian aircraft that tracked his satellite phone call. Zelimkhan Yandarbiyev succeeded him; military command rests with Maskhadov.
en.Yeltsin Grozni'de askerlere 'zafer' dedi: Yeltsin hailed 'victory' to the troops in Grozny; the campaign goes on.
en.Kremlin ateşkesten vazgeçti; Seçim önces: The Kremlin dropped the ceasefire; the war continues ahead of the election.
en.Seçime on hafta kala 'savaşı bitiren baş: Ten weeks before the vote, the 'president who ended the war' image is valuable. The army dislikes the ceasefire and the Chechens are gaining time.
en.Yandarbiyev ateşkesi imzaladı; Çeçen müf: Yandarbiyev signed the ceasefire; Chechen units regrouped.
en.Ateşkesi reddet, Grozni'ye hazırlan: Reject it and prepare for Grozny
en.Basayev ve Maskhadov gizlice Grozni plan: Basayev and Maskhadov are secretly preparing a plan for Grozny.
en.Ateşkes dinlenme ve yeniden toparlanma f: The ceasefire is a chance to rest and regroup; but Yeltsin may win the election and strike again afterwards.
en.27 Mayıs: Yeltsin Kremlin'de Yandarbiyev: 27 May: Yeltsin met Yandarbiyev in the Kremlin and a ceasefire and prisoner exchange were signed; the next day he flew to Chechnya to declare 'victory'. The strongest scene of his election campaign.
en.Rus topçusu şehre ateş açtı; sivil kayıp: Russian artillery opened fire on the city; civilian losses and anger in Moscow.
en.Yeltsin Lebed'i Çeçenistan'a gönderdi; o: Yeltsin sent Lebed to Chechnya; the army is bewildered.
en.Seçimi kazandınız ama Grozni'yi kaybediy: You won the election but are losing Grozny. Pulikovsky is ready to bomb the city; Lebed says the army cannot win the war.
en.Çeçen birlikleri Grozni'yi geri aldı; Ru: Chechen forces retook Grozny; the Russian garrison is surrounded.
en.Çeçen komutanlar Grozni'de güç gösterip: Chechen commanders showed strength in Grozny and made contact with Lebed.
en.Birkaç yüz savaşçı koca bir şehri geri a: A few hundred fighters retook a whole city: a symbolic disaster for the army. It is also a chance to sit at the table from strength.
en.6 Ağustos: Yeltsin'in yemin töreni günü: 6 August: on the eve of Yeltsin's inauguration Chechen forces infiltrated and stormed Grozny from three sides, trapping the 12,000-strong Russian garrison. General Pulikovsky issued an ultimatum to evacuate the city; Lebed, at the Security Council, favours peace.
en.Lebed–Maskhadov anlaşmasıyla Rus birlikl: Under the Lebed–Maskhadov deal Russian troops pulled out by the end of December.
en.Reddet, harekâta devam: Reject it and continue the war
en.Genelkurmay anlaşmayı reddetti; Lebed'in: The General Staff rejected the deal; Lebed's authority weakened.
en.Savaşı kazanamayacağınızı kabul eden bir: An agreement that admits the war cannot be won: Yeltsin's health is poor and the army is embittered, but the war's cost has become too high.
en.Çekilme karşılığı statünün ertelenmesi: Withdrawal in exchange for deferred status
en.Çeçenistan'da Rus birlikleri ülkeyi terk: Russian troops are leaving Chechnya; celebrations in Grozny.
en.Çeçen komutanlar 'statü ertelenemez' diy: Chechen commanders refused, saying 'status cannot be deferred'.
en.Savaşı fiilen kazandınız: Rus birlikleri: You have effectively won: Russian troops are leaving, but independence has not been recognised. The country is ruined, there is no economy and too many armed commanders.
en.Tiflis sınır birliklerini takviye ederek: Tbilisi reinforced border units and declared its neutrality.
en.Gürcistan'a Pankisi vadisinden mülteci a: Refugees began to flow into Georgia through the Pankisi Gorge.
en.Çeçenistan'ın güneyindeki sınır Gürcista: The border south of Chechnya touches Georgia. Because of Abkhazia and South Ossetia, Shevardnadze must balance with Moscow.
en.31 Ağustos: Lebed ve Maskhadov Dağıstan': 31 August: Lebed and Maskhadov signed a ceasefire and withdrawal accord in the Dagestani town of Khasavyurt: Russian troops will leave and Chechnya's status is deferred to 31 December 2001. The first war effectively ended.
en.Maskhadov Moskova'yla ekonomik işbirliği: Maskhadov seeks economic cooperation with Moscow.
en.Bağımsızlık söylemini koru, Türkiye ve K: Insist on independence; turn to Turkey and the Gulf
en.Grozni diaspora ve Körfez bağışçılarıyla: Grozny courts the diaspora and Gulf donors.
en.Savaşın galibisiniz; şimdi devlet kurma: You are the victors; now comes the test of state-building. Armed commanders (Basayev, Raduyev) and radical Wahhabi groups will compete with you.
en.27 Ocak 1997: AGİT gözetiminde yapılan Ç: 27 January 1997: Aslan Maskhadov, the military commander, won the Chechen presidential election held under OSCE observation. Moscow accepted the vote as free but did not recognise independence.
en.Kremlin antlaşmayı imzaladı; bir 'ortak: The Kremlin signed; a joint commission will be set up.
en.Moskova ödeneklerini kesti; Çeçenistan'd: Moscow cut subsidies; unemployment in Chechnya is rising.
en.Savaş ağır sonuçlandı; ordu yeniden yapı: The war ended badly; the army is restructuring under budget pressure. The treaty is an 'honourable exit' for Moscow.
en.Maskhadov antlaşmayı imzaladı; Çeçenista: Maskhadov signed; Chechnya is seen internationally as a de facto state.
en.Maskhadov imzadan önce tanınma talebini: Before signing, Maskhadov repeated his demand for recognition.
en.Kremlin'in sizi 'eşit' görmesi büyük sem: The Kremlin treating you as 'equal' is a big symbolic win; yet Russia keeps the border shut and kidnappings and bandits damage the country's name.
en.Barış ve İlişkilerin İlkeleri Antlaşması: Treaty on Peace and the Principles of Relations
en.12 Mayıs 1997: Yeltsin ve Maskhadov Krem: 12 May 1997: Yeltsin and Maskhadov signed in the Kremlin a treaty on mutual renunciation of force. For Yeltsin the war is over; the Chechens read the text as Russia treating them as an independent state.
